extensions.platform: Android (Expo SDK 57, React Native). Sizes are dp/sp. Tokens live in theme/tokens.ts and are read with useTokens(). One dark world only.

display.purpose: Session name on the workout card; exercise name on its photo fade.

title.purpose: Section, bar and sheet titles; the KCAL LEFT unit.

label.purpose: Chips, segments, field labels, small actions.

overline.purpose: Data labels, units, the date line, status tags. Never a kicker.

numHero.purpose: Calories left, fasting clock, ruler value.

numLarge.purpose: Macro columns, rest clock, stats, volumes.

motion.name: base
motion.purpose: Default state transitions: chips, fields, nav pill, disclosure.

motion.name: slow
motion.purpose: Sheets and snackbars entering, story segment fills.

motion.name: pressSpring
motion.purpose: Touch feedback only (0.97 press scale, segmented indicator).

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Replaces every movement when the system removes animations.

imagery.name: exercise-photos
imagery.note: Loaded at runtime and cached on disk; start and end positions.

imagery.name: app-icon-and-splash

narrative.overview:
NutriLens is a training app first, and it looks like the best of its category: a black ground, graphite surfaces, off-white ink, and a single volt accent that means "act, progress, now". The next workout is the hero of every day; inside a session each exercise fills the screen with its demo photo fading into black, its name set in condensed Anton capitals on that fade, and logging a set is one large volt tap. Calories and macros sit one glance below the training, told in the same big Anton numerals.

The system plays the category standard straight rather than inventing a private metaphor. Density is generous where the hand is busy (64dp set rows, 56dp dock buttons, 48dp minimum targets for sweaty hands under gym light) and compact where the eye only checks (tracked 12sp labels, slim progress lines). It is dark only: black with white and volt ink holds up under gym fluorescents, in a dark room at night and in daylight glare, so there is no light scheme.

Motion serves feedback, never decoration: exponential ease-out at 160, 220 and 320ms for state changes, a quick spring only under the finger, numbers that count to their value, bars that grow once, horizontal page slides between exercises. When the system asks for reduced motion, every one of these becomes an instant cut or a crossfade.
keyCharacteristics: Black ground, graphite tonal layers, no decorative color.
One volt accent for every action, every progress fill and the current set.
Selection is inverted ink: white pill, black text.
Anton uppercase for titles and every big number; Inter for words and small data.
Full-bleed exercise photography fading into the ground.
Pills for actions, 20dp corners on photo cards, 14dp on containers.
Story bars carry progress across a session, a week, a questionnaire.

rules.name: The One Volt Rule
rules.body: Volt means act, progress or now: buttons, fills, the current set, done stamps. It never decorates, never fills a background panel, and never marks selection or data.

rules.name: The Inverted Selection Rule
rules.body: What the user has chosen turns white with black ink. A selected chip or segment is never volt.

rules.name: The Data Ink Rule
rules.body: Coral, sky and lilac belong to protein, carbs and fat. Nothing else borrows them, and they never sit on a button.

rules.name: The Graphite Calm Rule
rules.body: Things that are merely present (the active nav destination, past days, completed-but-not-current bars, the burn strata of the plan) step through graphite, so the one volt element on screen stays findable at a glance.

rules.name: The Anton Numbers Rule
rules.body: Titles and every number meant to be read at a glance are Anton capitals. Anton never sets a sentence, a caption or a label.

rules.name: The Tracked Label Rule
rules.body: Overline labels name data, units or state next to the thing they describe. They are never a decorative kicker stacked above a heading.

rules.name: The Heavy Capitals Rule
rules.body: Buttons speak in ExtraBold tracked capitals at 14 to 15sp; nothing else in the UI shouts in Inter capitals except overline labels.

rules.name: The Gutter Rule
rules.body: Content aligns to the 20dp gutter; only photography and the workout band are allowed to run past it.

rules.name: The Flat Black Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat; a raised thing is a lighter graphite, not a shadow. A second shadowed element needs a reason as strong as floating over scroll.

rules.name: The Fade-To-Ground Rule
rules.body: Photographs end in the ground color through a gradient so Anton text can sit on them: the workout card fades from clear to 94% black, the exercise page fades its lower 40% fully into the ground.

rules.name: The Pill-For-Action Rule
rules.body: If it is pressed to do something, it is a pill or a circle; rectangles with soft corners are containers.

dos: **Do** read every color from useTokens(); screens never hold raw hex.
**Do** keep one volt element as the obvious next action on each screen (START WORKOUT, LOG SET, the camera FAB).
**Do** set titles and glance numbers in Anton capitals and everything else in Inter.
**Do** fade photographs into the ground (#0A0A0A) before placing text on them.
**Do** keep touch targets at 48dp or more, and 56dp for the action used mid-set.
**Do** use exponential ease-out at 160, 220 or 320ms for state changes and swap to instant cuts or crossfades when animations are removed.
**Do** show selection as a white pill with black ink.
donts: **Don't** use volt for selection, decoration, backgrounds or data series.
**Don't** use coral, sky or lilac for anything but protein, carbs and fat.
**Don't** add a light scheme; Kinetic Black is dark only.
**Don't** add shadows to cards, sheets or buttons; only the floating FAB casts one.
**Don't** set sentences, captions or labels in Anton, or buttons in mixed case.
**Don't** stack an overline label above a heading as a decorative kicker.
**Don't** recolor the owner's app icon to match the palette.
